message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo, fought on 18 June 1815, was one of the bloodiest single engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  While exact figures vary depending on the source and how “casualties” are counted (killed, wounded, missing, or captured), most modern historians agree on the following rough totals:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| **Allied (British, Dutch‑German, Prussian, etc.)** | 20 000–23 000 |
| **French** | 10 000–12 000 |
| **Total** | 30 000–35 000 |

These numbers include those killed, wounded, missing, and taken prisoner.  The battle’s high casualty toll was a major factor in the eventual collapse of Napoleon’s Grande Armée and the end of his reign.
